chapter_title: Concerning the Three Blows that befell the Enemy because of the Light
chapter_note: This is a remarkably clean substrate chapter — a compact, numbered three-fold eschatological teaching about three cosmic blows against the Enemy/Darkness. The entire structure (first war, second dissolution, third separation) maps cosmic process onto cosmic process with no contemporary application, no institutional content, no exhortation, and no citations. The only non-substrate material is the brief dialogue frame attribution in P1. Gardner's note about 'rudimentary redaction' in ch. 39-41 may refer to the sequence ordering rather than heavy editorial overlay within the chapter itself. The exhortation that Gardner mentions (exhorting the faithful despite persecution) is not present in the surviving text as given — it may have been in a lost section or may refer to the broader chapter context not included here. The oldest teaching layer is overwhelmingly dominant.

paragraphs.core_text: The Darkness itself, the enemy, has received three bad blows with three wars; and worse dangers from the light in those three wars.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again he turned, and says:' — dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula 'Once again he turned, and says:' is standard editorial attribution. The substantive content is a cosmological thesis statement that sets up the three-fold numbered teaching. Both sides (Darkness/enemy, light, three wars) are internal to the cosmic system. The thesis sentence defines the teaching structure and belongs to the oldest layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The first: (The enemy) was brought out to the middle and separated from his dark earth, whence he had departed. He was vanquished in that first war, caught and [bound] by the living soul.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. 'The first:' is the teaching structure marker. All terms are cosmic-systemic: 'the middle' (cosmic zone), 'dark earth' (realm of Darkness), 'living soul' (the captured light substance). Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. The 'living soul' is a personified cosmic entity — the light substance that binds the enemy in the first war.

paragraphs.core_text: The second blow is the time when he will be dissolved and melted, and he perishes in this great fire. He is destroyed and overthrown, from the images that are all by which he exists. And he will be gathered in [to the] fetter corresponding to his archetype, and be made like he was from the first beginning.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Pure cosmic-process vocabulary: 'dissolved and melted,' 'great fire,' 'images' (cosmic forms), 'fetter corresponding to his archetype,' 'first beginning.' The concept of being gathered into a fetter 'corresponding to his archetype' is deeply correspondential — the binding form mirrors the original cosmic form. This is eschatological substrate: describes what WILL happen within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The third blow that will befall the enemy is the 'rolling back' [at the] end when everything will be separated, and male will be divided [from] female. Now, the male will be bound in the lump, but the female [will be thrown] in to the tomb. For it will be divided [ ... by a great] stone in their midst, for generation upon generation, for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit. 'Rolling back' is a cosmic-eschatological technical term. Male/female division describes the separation of cosmic principles, not gendered persons. 'Lump' (βώλος) and 'tomb' (τάφος) are cosmic repositories — both Greek loanwords in Coptic suggesting technical cosmological terminology transmitted through the tradition. The 'great stone' dividing them is a cosmic boundary marker. 'For generation upon generation, for ever and ever' describes the permanence of the cosmic state — no audience address or imperative voice. The mild exhortation score (4.41) appears driven by the 'for ever and ever' formula, not by actual exhortatory content.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.106⟩ This is the way that the binding of the enemy will come about, in a fetter that is burdensome and strong, one from which there is never escape; because [they have achieved] his binding and bound him for ever. And they have achieved his being set apart, and he has been set apart for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding summary of the three-blow teaching. Recapitulates the cosmic binding and separation described in the three enumerations. Both sides remain entirely within the cosmic system: fetter, binding, being set apart — all describe cosmic processes applied to the cosmic enemy. No audience address, no contemporary application, no institutional reference. The summary closure is architecturally complete: three blows enumerated, then their combined result stated.
